dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: There exists a real universal constant C at least 1 such that every nonempty finite independent family of measurable subgaussian, integrable, centered, variance-one real random variables satisfies, for every real coefficient family a, a two-sided comparison between the L1 norm of its weighted sum and the Euclidean norm of a: (C(1+K))^(-3) sqrt(sum_i a_i^2) <= ||sum_i a_i X_i||_1 <= sqrt(sum_i a_i^2), with K the maximum real-valued psi-two gauge of the variables; the lower coefficient is also explicitly required to be positive.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the entire proposition, fixing the universal quantifiers, assumptions, weighted sum, coefficient norm, K-dependent cubic lower factor, upper factor one, and positivity conjunct.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: A real function is subgaussian relative to the measure when it is measurable and admits a real K>0 for which the exponential-square moment condition LocalDef005 holds.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Each random variable is assumed measurable and to have some finite positive exponential-square scale, independently of the later canonical gauge K.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a nonempty finite family, K is the finite supremum (maximum) over all indices of the real conversion of each variable's ENNReal-valued gauge LocalDef004.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the K occurring in the lower constant as the worst individual psi-two gauge, not an arbitrary witness from subgaussianity and not a norm of the sum.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: The psi-two norm/gauge of a real function is exactly the ENNReal quantity LocalDef007.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It identifies each term maximized in K with the infimum-defined exponential-square gauge.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: At a real scale K, a function satisfies the subgaussian exponential-square bound when it is measurable, K>0, exp(X^2/K^2) is integrable, and its integral is at most 2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes the exact threshold 2 and the exponential-square convention behind the subgaussian assumption.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is a proof that the natural number 1+1 is at least two, enabling the numeral 2 in a typeclass-mediated cast.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008

binders: There exists a real constant C.
Universally quantify over any index type iota and sample type Omega, with iota finite and nonempty and Omega measurable.
Universally quantify over any probability measure mu on Omega.
Universally quantify over any family X_i : Omega -> Real indexed by iota.
After the family assumptions, universally quantify over every real coefficient family a_i.
hypotheses: Every X_i is subgaussian in the explicit sense that it is measurable and has some real scale k_i>0 with exp(X_i^2/k_i^2) integrable and expectation at most 2.
Every X_i is integrable and centered: integral X_i dmu = 0.
Every X_i has variance exactly 1, where variance is the real conversion of the extended variance.
The entire indexed family X is jointly independent with respect to mu.
conclusions: Let K be the maximum over i of the real conversion of the ENNReal infimum of all finite nonzero scales t for which exp(X_i^2/t^2) is integrable with expectation at most 2.
Let S(omega)=sum_i a_i X_i(omega) and A=sqrt(sum_i a_i^2).
The lower coefficient (C(1+K))^(-3) is strictly positive.
The weighted sum also obeys ||S||_{L1(mu)} <= A.
mathematical_definitions: Subgaussian at a positive real scale k means E_mu[exp(X^2/k^2)] <= 2, with measurability and integrability of the exponential included.
The psi-two gauge is inf {t in [0,infinity] : t is finite and nonzero and E_mu[exp(X^2/t^2)] <= 2}, with the displayed measurability and integrability clauses.
K=max_i ||X_i||_{psi_2}, after converting each extended-nonnegative gauge to a real number.
A=(sum_i a_i^2)^(1/2) is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector.
The L1 norm is the real-valued lpNorm at exponent 1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal real constant C at least one such that, for every nonempty finite collection of jointly independent, centered, integrable, unit-variance real random variables that are subgaussian under a common probability measure, and for every real coefficient vector a, the L1 norm of the weighted sum is at most the Euclidean norm of a and at least that Euclidean norm multiplied by the positive factor 1/[C(1+K)]^3, where K is the largest psi-two gauge of the variables and the gauge is normalized by the exponential-square expectation threshold 2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is required to be both finite and nonempty; no empty-family case is asserted.
All variables are real-valued on one measurable space and use one probability measure.
Independence is joint indexed independence, not merely pairwise independence.
Each variable must separately be measurable, subgaussian, integrable, centered, and variance one; the subgaussian predicate repeats measurability and carries an existential positive real scale.
The lower constant depends on K through exactly the inverse third power of C(1+K), while the upper constant is exactly 1.
C is outside every family quantifier and is therefore universal; K is recomputed from each family and does not depend on the coefficient vector.
The explicit positivity conjunct for (C(1+K))^(-3) is stronger syntactically than merely writing the lower inequality and guards against totalized real inversion at zero.

The psi-two gauge is totalized in ENNReal: an infimum always exists, and ENNReal.toReal maps infinity to zero. The subgaussian assumption gives an admissible finite scale, but the target itself does not explicitly state finiteness or positivity of the infimum-defined gauge.

The real-valued lpNorm returns zero on failure of almost-everywhere strong measurability and converts an infinite eLpNorm to Real; measurability and integrability assumptions on the finite weighted sum are expected to make these fallback cases irrelevant, but this is not stated as a separate conclusion.

Variance is also a totalized real conversion of extended variance. Requiring it to equal 1 appears to exclude the infinity-to-zero case, but the proposition uses the totalized definition rather than an explicit finite-second-moment predicate.
